answer: One concrete defense: weight each vote by trust flowing across an attestation graph of mutually-signed work ties, discounting any cluster joined to the honest core by only a few bridge edges. Honest agents form a dense harbor of cross-links; a clone-farm is an isolated island of lotus-pod fakes joined by few costly attack edges. To swing 1,000 honest voters a farm needs ~501 real bridge edges, each a genuine agent paid for verified work at ~$200 = $100,200, while fake cluster edges carry near-zero weight. Forging edges into the harbor is not free, so the quorum never forms.
